title: Hand Washing, Side by Side
description: Film one of your team washing their hands, then say what you saw. I look at the same video and we compare. The point is not to catch anybody out — it is to find out whether you and I are reading the same wash the same way, because that is what an auditor standing in your kitchen will be doing.

questions.title: Record someone on your team washing their hands, start to finish.
questions.help: One take, no stopping. Start recording before the water goes on and keep going until they have used the sanitizer. If the clip starts with the water already running there is no way to tell how long the wash took, and that is half the standard. Hold the phone so the sink, their hands and the towels are all in shot.

questions.title: Watching that back: did they complete every step of hand washing properly?
choices: Yes — every step, start to finish
questions.help: Answer it before you read any list. The job in a real kitchen is spotting a miss without a sheet in your hand.

questions.title: Which steps did they miss? Tick every one.
choices: Washed at a dedicated hand wash sink, not a prep or dish sink
Wet their hands before the soap went on
Used antibacterial soap and worked up a lather
The whole wash took at least 20 seconds — wet, lather, rinse, dry
Dried with a single-use paper towel
Turned the faucet off with a paper towel, unless the sink is hands-free
questions.help: Tick what was missed, not what was done. If you are not sure one way or the other, leave it alone — we will compare notes either way.

questions.title: You must wash your hands when you arrive at work.
questions.explanation: First thing, every shift, before you touch anything.

questions.title: You must wash your hands before putting on gloves and each time you change gloves.
questions.explanation: Every time. A clean glove over a dirty hand is still a dirty hand.

questions.title: After using the restroom, you only need to wash your hands once.
questions.explanation: Twice. Once before you leave the restroom, then again at the back hand sink — you touched the door on the way out.

questions.title: It is acceptable to dry your hands on your apron if paper towels are unavailable.
questions.explanation: No. If there are no paper towels, that is the problem to fix — an apron undoes the whole wash.

questions.title: When do you have to wash your hands? Tick every one that counts.
choices: Before you put gloves on, and every time you change them
After handling money, trash or dirty dishes
After sneezing, coughing or blowing your nose
Only when your hands look dirty
questions.help: More than one is right. The list is on the poster above your hand sink.
questions.explanation: All four, and none of them are optional. Hands do not have to look dirty to be dirty — that is the whole reason the rule is a list of moments and not a judgement call.

questions.title: What is wrong with this picture?
choices: Every glove holder should have gloves in it
questions.explanation: Both glove holders are empty. A hand sink has to be stocked — towels, soap, sanitizer, and gloves within reach — or the wash stops at the point where somebody has to walk off to find a box.
